 Grayson Allen 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Grayson Allen accounted for 27 points (9-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and seven three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 After scoring 14 points on 4-of-18 shooting in Charlotte’s prior two games, Allen needed a night like Saturday. He shot a stellar 7-of-10 from beyond the arc, including 3-of-3 in an 11-point first quarter. The 27 points are a new season-high for Allen, who scored 20 or more in two of Charlotte’s first three games. He’ll have a higher fantasy ceiling until Coby White and Kon Knueppel are cleared to return from their injuries. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Dennis Schröder

 Dennis Schröder (foot) is questionable to play against the Wizards on Friday. 
 Schröder has been the starter with Coby White (calf) sidelined to start the year. If Schröder is unavailable, Sion James will likely take over point guard duties, with Grayson Allen entering the starting unit. Rookie Christian Anderson Jr. would also likely take on extra minutes off the bench, and there is a slight chance he starts. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Kneuppel (hamstring) is out for Monday’s game against the Wizards. 
 As of October 20, Knueppel, who had missed the entire preseason with a hamstring strain, had resumed on-court work. However, he still has not reached the point where he can play in games. While Sion James has started Charlotte’s first three games, Grayson Allen is the better option for fantasy managers looking for a streamer. 
 Grayson Allen 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Grayson Allen provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (6-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday. 
 Allen hasn’t started in place of Kon Knueppel (hamstring), but he has been able to fill the shooting void. That included a clutch four-point play in this game, which gave the Hornets a lead that they didn’t relinquish. Allen is rostered in just 33 percent of Yahoo! leagues, but with how many threes Charlotte shoots as a team, Allen should be rostered until Knueppel returns. 
 Sion James 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #4 
 The Charlotte Hornets will start Dennis Schroeder, Sion James, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid, and Moussa Diabate against the the Hawks on Friday. 
 Despite Grayson Allen having a real good game on Wednesday, Sion James is still the starter for this game. Given that Sion did start 19 games last year, it seems like he will stay in the starting lineup until players return to help balance out the starters. Grayson Allen can still be rostered in some spots until players start getting back, but he’ll be a streamer in most cases. 
 Grayson Allen 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Grayson Allen had 21 points (6-of-9 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and five three-pointers against the Nets on Wednesday. 
 With Kon Knueppel (hamstring) sidelined, the Hornets need Sion James and Allen to pick up the slack. James started, but scored just three points in 26 minutes. Meanwhile, Allen had 21 points and five three-pointers in 28 minutes off the bench. Allen is the preferred streaming option while Knueppel is sidelined. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) has been ruled out against the Nets on Wednesday. 
 Knueppel missed the preseason and will remain out for the season opener, though he has progressed to individual on-court work. Knueppel may return soon, but until then, Charlotte will turn to Grayson Allen and Sion James to fill the void, with Allen being the better streaming option for fantasy managers. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) will miss the preseason and be re-evaluated during the first week of the regular season. 
 Given how well Knueppel played as a rookie and the Hornets’ decision to move on from LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, Friday’s news gives his 2026-27 season a brutal start. At a minimum, the runner-up for Rookie of the Year will be sidelined for four weeks, and that’s just for him to be re-evaluated. According to the Hornets, Knueppel suffered the left hamstring injury during an offseason on-court activity. His absence boosts the early-season values of Brandon Miller and Coby White while also making Grayson Allen a more viable late-round option in drafts. 
 Grayson Allen 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #8 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Suns have traded Grayson Allen, Royce O’Neale and a 2033 first-round pick to the Hornets for Miles Bridges, a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick. 
 After three seasons in Phoenix, Allen is headed back to the Eastern Conference. While injuries limited him to 51 games, the veteran guard averaged a career-high 16.5 points, 3.8 assists and 3.1 three-pointers for the Suns last season. When available, Allen is one of the best three-point shooters in the league, and a solid defender as well. His addition gives the Hornets welcome perimeter depth, which is needed in the aftermath of LaMelo Ball being traded to the Timberwolves. However, availability concerns will affect where Allen is selected in most fantasy drafts. 
 Jordan Goodwin 
 PHX 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Jordan Goodwin (calf) is out for Game 4 against the Thunder on Monday. 
 Goodwin hasn’t played since he injured his calf five minutes into the series’ opening game. The 27-year-old guard was said to have been progressing in his recovery, but was still ruled out for Game 4. Collin Gillespie has replaced him in the starting lineup while Grayson Allen provides additional depth off the bench. 
 Jordan Goodwin 
 PHX 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Suns head coach Jordan Ott said Sunday that Jordan Goodwin (calf) is improving and should be questionable for Monday’s Game 4 against the Thunder. 
 Injured during the series opener, Goodwin did not play in Games 2 or 3. Collin Gillespie has moved into the starting lineup, and Grayson Allen’s return during Saturday’s Game 3 defeat gave the Suns additional depth on the perimeter. Goodwin is most impactful as a defender, giving Phoenix another option to throw at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

 Naz Reid recorded 14 points (4-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and one block in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Reid has been in a bit of a funk since Charlotte’s October 24 win over the Heat. Over his last four games, the Hornets’ forward has shot 35.1 percent from the field and 21.7 percent from beyond the arc while averaging 12.8 points per game. That’s not the production fantasy managers were hoping for, especially as the Hornets continue to play without Coby White and Kon Knueppel. Hopefully, Reid can turn things around next week, with the Hornets hosting the Pistons on Monday.

 Brandon Miller finished Saturday’s loss to the 76ers with 24 points (8-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers.
 Miller shot the ball better than he did in Friday’s loss to the Wizards, when he finished 7-of-24 from the field. This season, he’s shooting 37.7 percent from the field, nearly six percentage points lower than last season (43.5). Hopefully, the eventual returns of Coby White and Kon Knueppel will make things a bit easier for Miller by improving the quality of shots he gets in Charlotte’s offense. The Hornets play three games next week, starting with the Pistons on Monday.

 VJ Edgecombe tallied 10 points (4-of-13 FGs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Hornets.
 Edgecombe struggled offensively, but he did make two of his four three-point attempts. Add in the production in some other categories, and this could have been a much worse night for those rostering the 76ers’ guard. Unfortunately, Philadelphia doesn’t play again this week, but they do play four games next week with no back-to-backs.

 Adem Bona recorded two points (1-of-3 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in Saturday’s win over the Hornets.
 With Joel Embiid out, Bona moved into the starting lineup on Saturday. Unfortunately, he produced little, as foul trouble limited him to 22 minutes. Jabari Walker, who played 19 minutes, picked up the slack, finishing with 12 points, six rebounds and one three-pointer. The 76ers don’t have a back-to-back in their four-game Week 3, so Bona’s opportunities are likely to be limited.

 Jaylen Brown (knee) accounted for 16 points (6-of-15 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and two steals in Saturday’s win over the Hornets.
 Back in action after sitting out Friday’s win over the Knicks with left patellar tendinopathy, Brown played 38 minutes against the Hornets. Even with LeBron James and Joel Embiid out, the playing time was somewhat surprising, given the injury Brown was returning from. The good news is that Philadelphia’s schedule for next week doesn’t have a back-to-back. Hopefully, that bodes well for Brown’s availability.
